recordDecisions.title: Pseudolocality and strong uniqueness for complete Ricci flows
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Huang and Peng report uniform short-time pseudolocality and strong uniqueness for smooth complete Ricci flows whose initial metric has Ricci curvature bounded below and uniformly positive injectivity radius, without an a priori evolving curvature bound. Complete Ricci-flat metrics with positive injectivity radius are stationary, and every complete flat initial metric is stationary; this answers Chen’s Euclidean-space strong-uniqueness question in every dimension.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The authors explicitly attribute the main proof ideas to ChatGPT-6 Astra; they wrote the paper after absorbing and interacting over those ideas.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Audit entropy monotonicity, finiteness and time regularity without global curvature bounds, the point-picking/compactness passage and the flat-initial-metric corollary. Check exact correspondence to Chen’s historical question; this does not assert uniqueness from arbitrary complete initial metrics without the stated conditions. No independent specialist verification is established. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Primary version-one first-submission date, not manuscript drafting date.

recordDecisions.title: Generators of separable unital C*-algebras
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Elliott, Li and Niu report that, assuming the recent separable-predual II1-factor single-generation theorem, a separable unital C*-algebra with nonempty compact zero-dimensional extreme trace boundary has two ordinary generators under strict comparison of positive elements. With real rank zero and strict comparison of projections it is singly generated with norm-dense G-delta single generators. A separate atomless full-spectrum unitary and vanishing small-corner conditional-expectation compression hypothesis yields single generation, including reduced free-group C*-algebras for 2 through countably infinitely many generators.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The paper directly states that the work was carried out using ChatGPT; mathematical stages and exact model are not specified.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Audit the assumed II1-factor generation theorem and the precise small-corner compression hypothesis; a Haar unitary alone is explicitly insufficient. Establish theorem-level AI materiality, original priority and the claimed free-product applications. Do not generalize this to every separable C*-algebra or confuse two ordinary with two self-adjoint generators. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Primary version-one first-submission date, not manuscript drafting date.

recordDecisions.title: An elementary proof of geometric bulk conductances in even dimensions
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Drouot reports an independent elementary proof of the recent Martinian–Stoiber geometric Kubo conductance identity in every even dimension: for the stated short-range projectors and transverse open-set families, geometric conductance is the topological intersection integer times bulk conductance. The proof deforms cochains using Stokes, Poincare and Kitaev’s algebraic identity, rather than newly discovering the already-reported conductance formula.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The author explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5 with almost the entire proof and describes his removal of an unnecessary part and subsequent organization.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Audit decay, trace-class and transversality hypotheses and the elementary cochain argument. Compare against Martinian–Stoiber to establish genuine independent proof novelty and chronology, not priority for the identity itself; the earlier theorem was learned of late. No independent proof review is established. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Primary version-one first-submission date, not manuscript drafting date.

recordDecisions.title: Improved spectral counts for x1²+x2²−x3²=D
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Baier reports smooth even weighted counts with weight Phi(x3/M), support in [-2,2] and 1<=M<=sqrt(D). For D=n² and both x3 parities the error is O(n^(1+7/64+epsilon)M^(-1/2)), nontrivial for M>=n^(71/96+epsilon). For D=f²D0 with odd fundamental D0 the error is O(D^epsilon f^(1+7/64)D0^(2/3)M^(-1/2)); for D congruent 5 modulo 8 this gives all solutions and range M>=D^(4/9+epsilon).
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Section 1.6 attributes the spectral/geodesic approach, Hecke reductions, principal theorems and parity/Eisenstein calculations to Claude Opus 5.5 High, under Baier’s problem setting, requirements and evaluation.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Check main-term normalization, parity and fundamental-discriminant restrictions, Hecke relations and spectral inputs. These are weighted asymptotics, not unrestricted unweighted counts; conditional Lindelof/Ramanujan improvements are not unconditional conclusions. Reconcile the earlier paper’s corrected main term and establish independent verification. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Primary version-one first-submission date, not manuscript drafting date.

recordDecisions.title: Orbit strata and smooth topology of positively curved six-manifolds
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Gao and Liu report refined orbit stratifications for closed simply connected positively curved six-manifolds with effective isometric SO(3) or SU(2) actions: nine necessary boundaryless SO(3) weighted-graph families, equivariant classification in cyclic-exceptional cases, sphere-bundle and nonspin odd-integer families for specified ball quotients, a CP3 case, and SU(2) identifications with the Eschenburg flag or weighted S2xS4 actions. They deduce rational ellipticity in this symmetry class and restricted diagonal-product curvature obstructions.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The primary abstract says some results were discovered by ChatGPT-6-astra and verified by the authors.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Identify exactly which results were AI-discovered; audit standing hypotheses, reconstruction and characteristic-class formulas. Keep graph restrictions, smooth realizability and positive-curvature realizability separate. The source expressly does not rule out arbitrary invariant metrics on all remaining candidate actions; author checks are not independent expert verification. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Primary version-one first-submission date, not manuscript drafting date.

recordDecisions.title: Language modeling and monotone compression
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Mazor and coauthors report an equivalence between next-token language modeling and order-preserving compression up to additive constant error, a cryptographic characterization of when the monotonicity requirement can be omitted using infinitely-often one-way functions, and an equivalence between next-bit pseudoentropy and monotone incompressibility under their stated efficiency and distribution conditions.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The disclosure says generative AI reviewed technical proof correctness and suggested fixes, as well as editing the overview; the authors retain origination of all results.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Determine which technical fixes were adopted and whether AI’s mathematical contribution was material rather than only review or rewriting. Audit computational quantifiers, distribution assumptions and the additive-constant reductions. Exact models are not disclosed; do not infer AI discovery from the paper’s subject. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Primary version-one first-submission date, not manuscript drafting date.

recordDecisions.title: Exact regret-profile frontier and finite-window prediction refinements
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Ozelim and coauthors report sharpenings and elementary additions to classical prediction theory. For a countable pairwise mutually singular source family, infinite-horizon expected log-loss regret profiles obey the Kraft inequality, every Kraft profile is attained by its subprobability Bayes mixture, and equality holds exactly for full-mass mixtures on every cylinder. The paper distinguishes these refinements from its many explicitly known results and does not prove that deployed language models perform Solomonoff induction.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The primary disclosure explicitly includes AI checking derivations and proposing objections, with all theorem origination attributed to the authors; model names and adopted mathematical changes are not specified.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Compare Theorem 2.7 and Appendix B’s equality/converse and leakage ledger against Hutter, Wald and earlier complete-class/log-loss results, as mapped in Appendix H. Establish exact novelty and whether derivation checking changed any mathematical result; most of the discussion is known theory. Do not count the survey’s known results as new AI discoveries. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Primary version-one first-submission date, not manuscript drafting date.

recordDecisions.title: Counterexamples in heterogeneous Hegselmann–Krause opinion dynamics
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Hegarty, Ognissanti and Wedin report explicit heterogeneous SBC and SBI opinion systems refuting Mirtabatabaei–Bullo’s eventual proximity-digraph freezing and eventual freezing-or-pseudostability conjectures, and the corresponding part of their published Theorem 6.4. The examples include convergent trajectories with indefinitely changing digraphs and constant-digraph trajectories that are not pseudostable. The main conjecture that every opinion vector converges remains open.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Section 7 explicitly says Claude Opus 5.5 found all four examples under author prompting; the human authors wrote the paper and checked the examples by hand.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Independently verify the exact closed-neighborhood update inequalities and trajectories and compare the cited 2012 assertions. Do not promote auxiliary-conjecture disproofs to a disproof of convergence, or treat unverified background computations mentioned in Section 7 as established classifications. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Primary version-one first-submission date, not manuscript drafting date.

recordDecisions.title: Smaller and near-homogeneous Hegselmann–Krause counterexamples
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: JD Jones reports new extensions beyond Hegarty–Ognissanti–Wedin: five-agent constant-digraph SBC and SBI counterexamples, a five-agent SBI complex-mode example oscillating about its limit in every five consecutive times, and a five-agent SBC family with unequal radii arbitrarily close to homogeneous that converges without freezing or pseudostability. A separate paper-only argument claims four or fewer agents with eventually constant digraph cannot have this behavior, so five is minimal in that restricted regime.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The owner disclosure credits Claude Opus 5.5/Fable 5.1 with exact search, proofs and formalization, and GPT-6 Pro consultation with the complex-mode, near-homogeneous and lower-bound extensions.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Independently check the exact models, invariant neighborhoods, complex eigenmodes and near-homogeneous parameter limits. The four-agent lower bound and some all-n/rate statements are paper-only, not Lean endpoints; no global minimum for nonfreezing digraphs or equal-radius counterexample is claimed. Establish novelty relative to the original paper’s unpublished computations and first repository visibility. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

recordDecisions.title: Möbius invariance of finite spherical Ramsey sets
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Will Strinz reports Theorem C extending OpenAI family 172: for a finite distinct point set on a unit sphere and a Lorentz transformation in O(1,d), the set is Ramsey if and only if its Lorentz-Möbius image is Ramsey, without an affine-spanning assumption. Corollaries concern images of algebraic spherical sets and the stated rational-parameter circle families.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The disclosure credits Claude Opus 5.5 with exploratory theorem/proof work and formal extensions, with Sonnet 5.5 literature and reproduction assistance under human direction.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Check the no-affine-spanning extension, sphere/Lorentz domains and which circle corollaries are formal. The identification with all classical Möbius transformations for d>=2 is cited, not formalized; the analogous dimension-one identification fails. No arbitrary-sphere similarity reduction or cross-ratio triangle classification is established. Distinguish the new extension from inherited OpenAI modules and record 3760. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

recordDecisions.title: Finite-regularity and certificate characterizations of electromagnetic source tensors
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Stephanie Alexander reports constructive finite-regularity characterizations in flat four-dimensional Lorentz space: a 210-coefficient homogeneous quadratic symmetric tensor ansatz is reduced to the Maxwell stress line by explicit covariance/trace or conservation certificates; globally C3 source-free conserved tensors have the stated 17-parameter family; an everywhere differentiable sourceful exchange law fixes the stress coefficient up to a constant tensor, with zero-field normalization selecting the Maxwell tensor. This is not a claim that Maxwell-stress uniqueness itself is new.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Primary metadata attributes mathematical research and proofs to human-directed OpenAI GPT-family Codex work, and Claude extraction/porting; exact model versions and theorem-level allocation are incomplete.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Compare the precise differentiability, conservation and sourceful hypotheses against Fock, Collinson, Lovelock, Kerrighan and Anco–Pohjanpelto; some full historical pages were not retrieved by the author. Audit the finite certificates and the sourceful exchange-law route. Establish novelty of the narrowed routes rather than rediscovery of stress uniqueness or the smooth 17-parameter consequence; no curved-space or new physical coupling is claimed. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

recordDecisions.title: Separated Euclidean distances below 0.74 n² in a fixed dimension
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: John Tripodo reports that for every integer n>=68000 there are n points in the single Euclidean space R^458999 with nonzero pair distances at least 1, distinct unordered non-diagonal pair distances separated by at least 1, and diameter strictly below (37/50)n². Neither the dimension nor constant is claimed optimal, and this is not a planar theorem.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The dated primary archive credits substantial OpenAI ChatGPT research/manuscript assistance under Tripodo’s direction; broader Claude use is disclosed without assigning particular proof steps.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Audit the fixed-dimension embedding, separation and explicit constants, and establish historical priority for this restricted Erdős 670 construction. Source-reported project rebuilds and compiled-import kernel replay on two machines do not establish source-only upstream builds or independent human review. Archive metadata says publication October12 but creation is October13; use October13 as first supported public archive observation unless earlier visibility is established. Do not create another row for the subsequent Palomar port. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Public archive created October13; metadata publication October12 retained as discrepancy.

recordDecisions.title: Structural bounds for codimension-one avoiding intersecting hypergraphs
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Linmiao Xu reports structural extensions for non-2-colourable intersecting r-uniform hypergraphs whose distinct edges meet in at most r-2 vertices: minimum active degree at least 3, active vertices at least 2r+1 for r>=3, degree at least 4 at a vertex in a multiple intersection, and 3|V|+1<=r|E| for r>=4. For r=4 the package gives at least nine edges and nine active vertices. It separately formalizes Alon’s and Price’s already-known resolutions of the main Erdős 836 questions, which are not newly credited here.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Primary metadata directly acknowledges AI-assisted proof development and statement/axiom audits; exact models and origination of each additional bound are not given.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Establish novelty of the sharpened handshake and nine-edge/nine-vertex bounds and identify which mathematical extensions, rather than ports of Alon, Price and Lovasz, were AI-assisted. Audit non-2-colourability, active-vertex and intersection hypotheses and standard-axiom statement correspondence. Do not label this a newly AI-discovered settlement of the main Erdős 836 questions. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
